rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope and a redundant conjunct; project retained. Schedule D (2025) lines 1b, 2, 3, 8b, 9 and 10 read “Totals for all transactions reported on Form(s) 8949 with Box A or Box G checked” and so on through Box F or Box L; lines 1a and 8a take the aggregate route for basis-reported transactions without adjustments. The second transcription includes the digital-asset boxes G–L as printed. The project filters on boxes A–F only because digital-asset transactions are refused (`sales.digital`, spec 2.2), so within scope the two sums are over the same entries. On lines 2, 3, 9 and 10 the project also requires the detail route; the second transcription omits that conjunct because the aggregate route is permitted only for boxes A and D and any other use is refused by `sales.bad_aggregate`, which makes the project's conjunct redundant rather than wrong. No change to the data; a future stage bringing digital assets into scope must widen these filters, and this ruling records that.

Ruling: equivalent within scope; project retained. The instruction (i1040gi p. 33, line 7a, Exception 1) requires Schedule D when any Form 1099-DIV has an amount in box 2b, 2c or 2d, which the second transcription tests on the raw boxes. The project tests the worksheet results instead; with no sales entered the worksheets have nothing to net against, so a nonzero box 2b or 2d gives a nonzero result, and box 2c is refused (`div.section1202`). When sales are entered Schedule D is required on that ground alone. If carryovers come into scope the netting could zero a worksheet result while a box amount remains, and the test must then move to the raw boxes; this ruling records that.
